title: Collision System Deep Dive 🧱
description: Master collision primitives, presets, channels, and trace responses.

slides.title: How Collision Works 🛡️
slides.content:
# The Invisible Shield

Collision defines how actors interact when they touch. Every actor has:

* **Collision Preset** – a template that sets up responses.
* **Object Type** – what this actor is (WorldStatic, Pawn, etc.).
* **Collision Responses** – how it reacts to other object types (Ignore, Overlap, Block).

You don't need separate "collision mesh" always; the engine uses the **simple collision** shapes you set up per mesh.

quizData.question: Which response type lets two actors pass through each other but fires events?
quizData.explanation: Overlap allows actors to interpenetrate but generates overlap events for triggers.

slides.title: Collision Presets 📋
slides.content:
## Quick Setup

In the Details panel → Collision → **Collision Presets**, choose from:

* **BlockAll** – stops everything
* **OverlapAll** – overlaps everything
* **Pawn** – blocks only pawns (players)
* **PhysicsActor** – interacts with everything as a physics object
* **Trigger** – overlaps all, useful for volumes
* **Custom…** – define your own response

Most props should be **BlockAll** (for walls) or **BlockAllDynamic** (for movable objects).

slides.title: Object Channels & Trace Channels 🎯
slides.content:
## Behind the Scenes

Under Project Settings → Collision, you can define **Object Channels** and **Trace Channels**.

* **Object Channels** – categories like WorldStatic, WorldDynamic, Pawn, Vehicle.
* **Trace Channels** – used for line traces (visibility, camera).

You can add custom channels (e.g., "Projectile", "Pickup") to fine‑tune interactions.

quizData.question: To make a volume that triggers events but does not block movement, set its Collision Preset to _____.
quizData.explanation: The Trigger preset sets responses to Overlap for all channels, so actors pass through and fire events.

slides.title: Collision Shapes 🔵🔺
slides.content:
## Simple vs Complex

For performance, always use **simple collision** in the mesh editor:

* Open a Static Mesh asset → **Collision** menu → **Add Sphere/Capsule/Box Simplified Collision**.
* These simple shapes are used for physics and collision detection.
* **Complex Collision** uses the actual mesh polygons – expensive, used only for specific ray‑casts.

Set **Collision Complexity** in the Details panel to **Use Simple Collision as Complex** for most cases.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Visualise Collision

In the viewport, click **Show → Collision** to see all collision shapes. This helps debug objects that don't block as expected.
